extracted.intended_audience: grant reviewers and molecular microbiology/biophysics researchers (investigators and collaborators)
extracted.subtask_description: Research plan and experimental standards for a grant proposal to study the agr quorum-sensing system in Staphylococcus aureus, covering structural/biophysical experiments, protein engineering, small-molecule screening, and vertebrate animal studies. The content specifies experimental designs, validation pipelines, animal-use protocols, and screening/assay workflows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crystallization strategy for dynamic constructs
rubrics_metrics.description: Because constructs that 'unleash' the CA domain are expected to have increased dynamics that could make crystallization challenging, structural studies will be pursued in parallel on corresponding GCN4-DHp constructs which are expected to be less dynamic but still informative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If dynamic constructs fail to crystallize, use engineered/chimeric constructs (e.g., GCN4-DHp) that reduce dynamics while preserving the surfaces exposed/occluded between off- and on-states; crystallographic success of one GCN4-DHp construct trapped in the 'on-state' is encouraging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-molecule FRET experiment design
rubrics_metrics.description: Study AgrC dynamics using single-molecule FRET (smFRET) with a TIRF microscope set-up and GCN4-AgrC chimeric constructs to compare constructs that mimic various activity states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform smFRET in collaboration with an expert lab (Haw Yang). Exploit dimeric nature and trans autophosphorylation of constructs. Compare constructs spanning activity series to enable rigorous physical modeling of active-state characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fluorophore labeling scheme for smFRET
rubrics_metrics.description: An ALEXA 555 donor fluorophore will be incorporated into the DHp of one protomer using cysteine chemistry and an ALEXA 647 acceptor into the CA domain of the other protomer. Several pairwise combinations will be tested for optimal FRET response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the crystal structure of the AgrC cytoplasmic domain to guide fluorophore placement. Mix the two species and perform a refolding protocol to produce a statistical mixture (≈50% donor-acceptor pairs); components with only one probe should be silent in the assay.

rubrics_metrics.name: FRET data interpretation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Predicted FRET behaviors: the 'off-state' construct is expected to primarily exhibit a single FRET state with occasional excursions, whereas more active constructs will exhibit more complex FRET behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze changes in dwell time in given states and the number/distribution of FRET states observed as indicators of activity-state-dependent CA-DHp interactions; model time-dependent FRET behavior to infer physical characteristics of active/inactive kinase states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engineering AgrC ATP affinity (Km-ATP modification)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systematically mutate the G1 box and, if necessary, second-shell residues in AgrC-I to lower Km-ATP and increase ATP affinity; employ ROSETTA design tools if required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the AgrC-nanodisc system as the workhorse for protein-engineering studies. Once engineered, introduce the altered AgrC into an appropriate S. aureus genetic background using established methods and test the prediction that agr response will be less down-regulated during stress phases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peptide array strategy to identify a global agr activator
rubrics_metrics.description: Generate spatially defined arrays of AIP analogs using SPOT peptide synthesis on nitrocellulose functionalized with a bifunctional linker (aryl hydrazine + azide), with each peptide outfitted with an N-terminal PEG spacer and a propargyl group, then anchored by click chemistry and converted to thiolactone-containing immobilized AIPs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immobilization must preserve agonist activity (preliminary data show immobilized AIP-I can still activate agr in reporter cells). This approach allows rapid generation of hundreds of diverse AIP analogs for screening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary ELISA readout for peptide-array activation
rubrics_metrics.description: Use AgrC nanodiscs together with anti-pHis antibodies in an ELISA format: activation of AgrC by an immobilized peptide will lead to autophosphorylation which can be read out by ELISA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hits identified on the array should be resynthesized and verified using established in vitro and cell-based assays as part of a high-throughput validation workflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affinity-based small-molecule screening (ASMS) workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform ASMS by mixing pooled compound mixtures with AgrC-I-nanodiscs, resolving complexes by size-exclusion chromatography (SEC), and identifying target-associated compounds by LC-MS/MS (UPLC-Orbitrap).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Group pools by mass for MS deconvolution. Include competition controls (presence/absence of saturating AIP-I). Pilot studies on ~50,000 compounds identified AIP-competitive binders; plan to scale to full collection (millions/commercial libraries) available at the Screening Center.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secondary binding assay: fluorescent AIP displacement
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a dimethylamino-phthalimide labeled AIP assay to quantitatively measure specific binding of ligands to the AgrC sensor domain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply this quantitative binding assay as a secondary screen to measure sensor affinity of initial hits from SEC-based ASMS before proceeding to functional assays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead validation and optimization pipeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Validate ASMS/array hits by assaying compounds for activation or inhibition of AgrC autokinase activity using established biochemical and cell-based assays; use validated leads as starting points for medicinal chemistry to improve potency and efficacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor improvements using the in vitro and cell-based assays described; anticipate iterative cycles of chemical optimization guided by these functional readouts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of collaborators and screening/biophysics facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage expertise and instrumentation through collaborations: single-molecule biophysics with Professor Haw Yang (TIRF, instrumentation) and compound screening with the Princeton Small Molecule Screening Center (compound libraries and screening infrastructure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document letters of collaboration and make use of center resources (compound collections, instrumentation, technical expertise) to execute high-throughput and specialized assays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification for vertebrate animal use
rubrics_metrics.description: The studies are pre-clinical trials of therapeutic agents and therefore can be done only with live animals; mice are used as the 'lowest' vertebrate suitable for such studies and invertebrate models are not believed to translate satisfactorily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that the imaging system enables a 5–10-fold reduction in animal numbers compared with point-by-point enumeration methods; provide justification that vertebrate use is necessary for these experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal species, age, and strain specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Animals will be 8 or 12 week-old outbred Swiss-Webster mice of either sex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify age/strain/sex for each experiment and ensure consistency with protocol descriptions and ethical approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mouse deep quadriceps (DQ) infection model parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliver three infecting doses (10^7, 10^8, 10^9 bacteria) plus cytodex beads in 25 µl PBS; image animals daily to evaluate persistence and localization of infection; 27 mice proposed for this validation study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use daily imaging to reduce animal numbers and to determine reproducible attenuation endpoints; euthanize and enumerate viable bacteria at study completion to correlate imaging with bacterial counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mouse kidney abscess model parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine a reproducible kidney abscess-inducing dose by IV injection of graded doses (10^7, 10^8, 10^9) with 3 mice per dose, evaluated by IVIS imaging daily for 5 days (9 mice for validation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these graded-dose pilot studies to select doses for efficacy testing of small molecules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Toxicity testing parameters (IV)
rubrics_metrics.description: IV toxicity testing of the 4 most effective small molecules at 500 µg/mouse (20 mg/kg); mice will be monitored for signs of toxicity (ataxic gait, decreased activity, ruffled fur, weight loss, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate group sizes (text indicates 6–8 week old mice per test, 12 total) and monitoring schedules; escalate or adjust dosing based on observed toxicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pharmacokinetics sampling protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Perform pharmacokinetics with three 12-week-old Swiss-Webster mice of either sex per experiment; anesthetize, cannulate the femoral vein, inject 100 µl of test SM in PBS, withdraw 20 µl samples at 15-minute intervals for 90 minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these sampling intervals to profile early distribution/clearance; ensure appropriate anesthesia and surgical technique for serial sampling.

rubrics_metrics.name: In vivo efficacy testing and group-size rules for agr inhibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Correlation test: use 50 µg/mouse of each of the 4 SMs with 5 mice each for agr+ and agr− bacteria and 5 untreated controls (with option to use 4× dose if attenuation not reproducible). Imaging at 24 h intervals for 5 days, euthanize, and enumerate bacteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reproducible attenuation is not observed, increase dose. For kidney model efficacy use 10 mice (5 treated, 5 untreated). For repeated dosage and delayed administration follow specified group-size/regimen plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synergy testing with antibiotics
rubrics_metrics.description: Test SM synergy with vancomycin in the DQ model using groups of 20 mice: 5 with SM (2 mg/kg), 5 with vancomycin (33 mg/kg), 5 with both, and 5 untreated, with treatment at 0, 24, or 48 h post infection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the agr-attenuation hypothesis is substantiated, repeat synergy tests with the most effective agr inhibitor; include controls and pre-specified dosing regimens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal welfare, veterinary care, and housing standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Animals are housed in micro isolator cages, 5 mice per cage, in a room with proper ventilation, temperature control, light-dark cycle, and standard diet with water ad libitum; cages changed weekly by facility staff; dead animals autoclaved or dissected for viable counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow facility protocols for housing, cage changes, injections (IV/IP 100 µl, IM 25 µl), and disposal. Ensure veterinary oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimization of pain and distress
rubrics_metrics.description: Anesthetize animals with isoflurane for injections and imaging. Infected animals will receive ibuprofen at 7.5 mg/kg in drinking water; if discomfort persists, administer buprenorphine 0.05–0.1 mg/kg subcutaneously every 12 hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement analgesia protocols proactively and escalate analgesia per veterinary recommendations if animals remain in discomfort despite ibuprofen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Euthanasia method and humane endpoints
rubrics_metrics.description: Animals will be euthanized by CO2 narcosis at the end of experiments or during experiments if they show signs of severe morbidity (ruffled fur, ataxic gait); CO2 narcosis is the standard method recommended by the AVMA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define moribund criteria clearly in protocols and apply euthanasia promptly to minimize suffering; document endpoints and procedures for regulatory review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximum animal numbers and contingency planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Maximum number of mice for the proposed sets of experiments is stated as up to 440 (including screening of additional small molecules or AIP derivatives); testing of additional SMs would require 20 mice each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide maximum animal numbers for protocol approvals and use pilot data/imaging to reduce numbers where possible; include contingency plans if screening fails to identify effective compounds.
